messages:
nina_peopleops: Hey team — custody changed last week (shared custody settled 2026-05-02). Need to add my 8yo to my benefits on alternating weeks and confirm premium proration and FSA dependent care eligibility. Do we support split-week coverage or do I need to pick one subscriber?

sam_benefits: Congrats on resolution. Shared custody is a QLE. Insurance cannot typically toggle week-by-week — enrollment is per subscriber record. You can enroll the child on your plan and note custody arrangement, but carriers rarely do alternating-week billing.

olivia_payroll: For premiums, we set effective date to the QLE date (2026-05-02) and prorate per pay period. If you were previously covering the child under your ex's plan, we can coordinate termination and avoid overlap. Any premiums paid to the other carrier remain with them; we cannot retro-bill carriers.

kyle_legal: For FSA dependent care, eligibility depends on tax rules and child residency. If the child is in your custody at least part-time, you may still qualify but must follow IRS rules (custody tie-breaker). Recommend saving the custody order when you submit the QLE.

benefits-bot: Submit QLE here: https://benefits.redwood.com/qle. Choose "Change in custody", attach signed custody order and child's birth certificate. Deadline: 60 days from event (2026-05-02).

nina_peopleops: If I enroll now, how will retro premium be handled if ex had coverage through 5/04 and mine starts 5/02?

sam_benefits: We will set effective date 5/02. If your payroll already deducted insurance for 5/01-5/15, we calculate daily proration and issue adjustment: either payroll credit or spread deduction. We also reach out to your ex's carrier to confirm termination date to prevent double coverage.

olivia_payroll: Provide employee ID and QLE confirmation. We'll add adjustment code BEN-QLE-CUSTODY on the stub. Retro adjustments are itemized and non-taxable in most cases.

nina_peopleops: Filing QLE now and uploading custody order. Thanks for the clarity! :pray:
